feature: Double-click beside a range clears it
summary: A double-click on the ruler or the scrub bar anywhere outside the marked range clears it, whether you drew it or set it with I and O, and the playhead lands where you clicked. Escape on the timeline and a Clear Range row on the range's right-click clear it too.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording in Edit mode with the timeline showing.

try.do: Press I at 0:03 and O at 0:05 on the timeline, then click the ruler once at 0:06.
Drag along the ruler from 0:03 to 0:05, then double-click inside the green band.
Drag a range again, right-click on it and choose Clear Range.
Drag a range again and double-click the transport's scrub bar near its end.

evaluate: Does a double-click beside the range clear it every time you expect it to?
Is it right that a single click beside marks set with I and O still leaves them, as Premiere does?
Is Escape clearing the range when the timeline has the keyboard what you want, or should Escape keep only letting go of a pick?
Should the right-click row on a range read Clear Range, or keep Premiere's name Clear In and Out?
rough: Escape clears the range when the timeline has the keyboard (after any click in the timeline), not by where the pointer rests. Every other timeline key follows that same rule.
Right-clicking inside the range shows Clear Range in place of Clear In and Out. Outside it the row still says Clear In and Out. Both use Option-X.
A single click beside a range you just drew still clears it straight away, as before, so on a drawn range the second click of a double-click has nothing left to do.
Nothing new is drawn, so there is no mock frame to compare against: only a menu row name changed.
